title: JPMorgan Chase reveals data breach, but says it’s unrelated to this week’s banking outage
html:
JPMorgan Chase says its third-party vendors suffered a cyberattack, exposing marketing data like customer names and email addresses. The confirmation follows a report from Cybernews, which says a ransomware group leaked email addresses belonging to around 16,000 JPMorgan Chase customers.

JPMorgan Chase reveals data breach, but says it’s unrelated to this week’s banking outage

The data breach may have impacted customer names and emails, JPMorgan Chase says.

In a post about the attack, JPMorgan Chase says “there is no connection” to the outage that occurred earlier this week, which the company attributed to a “software bug:”

We have learned that third parties who provide services to the firm were the target of a cyber attack. Based on our investigation so far, we believe the attackers accessed certain marketing data held by those vendors, which may include some customer names and email addresses.

There is no disruption to our services. Where appropriate, we will contact affected customers directly and offer support, including complimentary credit monitoring. There is no connection to service disruption some customers experienced earlier this week.

As reported by Cybernews, the leaked dataset appears to include information linked to JPMorgan Chase’s invitation-only Reserve program. The hacking group claiming responsibility for the breach says it targeted Visa as well, which confirmed an attack on a third-party vendor in the Asia Pacific, Cybernews reports.

“Visa’s systems were not involved and were not impacted,” a Visa spokesperson tells Cybernews. “There is no indication that payment data such as card numbers have been affected.” Cybernews says it uncovered exposed data connected to 6,000 premium Visa customers. Visa didn’t immediately respond to The Verge’s request for comment.
